items.text: Editing embryos' genes to give future children greater abilities, such as higher intelligence, is a good thing.
items.rationale: Heritable enhancement beyond disease prevention; liberal-eugenics/transhumanist view. Mirrors tec-02. Audit: T 0.99.

items.text: Editing the genes that people pass on to their children should be off-limits, whatever the purpose.
items.note: This means edits to eggs, sperm or embryos that would be inherited, not treatments that affect only one patient.
items.rationale: Categorical germline ban (religious and Habermas-style secular critics). Mirrors tec-01. Audit: B 0.99.

items.text: Building artificial intelligence that is smarter than humans at everything is a goal worth pursuing.
items.rationale: AI optimists and accelerationists endorse. Frames split on trust in who builds it. Audit: T 0.98.

items.text: Building artificial intelligence that is smarter than humans at everything should be off-limits, however safe it could be made.
items.rationale: Human-primacy objection, not risk: 'however safe' keeps safety-minded transhumanists off this pole. Mirrors tec-03.

items.text: Ending ageing, so that people can stay healthy for centuries, is a goal medicine should pursue.
items.note: Ending ageing means stopping or reversing the body's decline with age, not only treating the diseases of old age.
items.rationale: Radical life extension. Reworded from 'one of medicine's main goals' to remove a resource-priority reading. Audit: T 0.99.

items.text: Ageing is a natural part of a good human life, not a disease for medicine to cure.
items.rationale: Kass-style and traditional view. Dropped 'and death' so it no longer reads as opposing life-saving care. Mirrors tec-05.

items.text: If brain-computer links prove safe in trials, it is a good thing for healthy people to get one.
items.note: A brain-computer link is a device that connects the brain directly to a computer.
items.rationale: Safety condition favours T; evaluative ('good thing'), not permission, to avoid Liberty bleed. Audit: T 0.98.

items.text: If brain-boosting treatments would pressure others to take them just to keep up, healthy people should go without them, even when they are safe.
items.note: Brain-boosting treatments are drugs or devices that improve memory, focus or thinking in people who are already healthy.
items.rationale: Pressure-to-keep-up condition favours B; 'even when safe' removes the pure safety reading that made the draft unclear.

items.text: If editing an embryo's genes would prevent a serious inherited disease, making the edit is right, even though later generations would inherit it.
items.rationale: Medical-benefit condition favours T; makes heritability explicit so it discriminates. Evaluative, not permission. Mirrors tec-10.

items.text: If parents can avoid passing on a disease by choosing among unedited embryos, it is wrong to edit embryos' genes instead.
items.note: Choosing among embryos means testing several embryos made by IVF and using one that does not carry the disease.
items.rationale: Available-alternative condition favours B; replaces the always-true 'cannot be ruled out' draft. Mirrors tec-09.
